title: Retail analytics at scale: 2.3M order lines, eight report pages
company: Contoso (fictional electronics retailer: 73 stores plus online)
buyer: CEO, CFO, head of retail and e-commerce
question: Why did sales fall in 2025 when order volume barely moved?
summary: A full retail model on the public Contoso sample: 2,349,091 order lines, 104,990 customers and 2,517 products over 2016-2025, modelled in dbt and reported in Power BI, with an AI-drafted annual review checked against the numbers.
workflow: Download the public Contoso sample (pinned by checksum) and load it into DuckDB
dbt builds a star schema over 2,349,091 order lines, with relationship and uniqueness tests
Power BI project: eight pages covering trend, products, customers, geography, stores, channel and cohorts
Claude drafts the annual trading review from computed facts only
Every number in the review is checked against the facts before it is shown

note.title: Annual trading review
note.markdown:
## 2025 trading review

**Sales fell 7.7% to $299.9M in 2025 (from $325.0M), and are now 33.3% below the 2023 peak of $449.5M.** The cause is spend per order, not demand: orders slipped only 1.2% (161,802 vs 163,695), while average order value dropped 6.6% to $1,853.79 from $1,985.63. It was $2,290.73 in 2023.

**Where it came from.** The United States drove the decline: sales there fell 20.5% to $126.3M from $158.8M, more than the whole company's drop. Germany grew 14.0% to $46.7M and Canada grew 5.7% to $40.8M. By category, TV and Video fell 35.9% to $26.8M and Home Appliances fell 16.3% to $46.9M, both big-ticket ranges, which fits the lower order value. Cameras and camcorders grew 30.2% and Audio grew 26.8%, from smaller bases.

**What held up.** Gross margin was steady at 56.0% (55.9% in 2024), so this is a volume-and-mix problem, not a pricing one. Active customers were 60,109 against 61,659.

**Channel mix.** Online was 55.3% of sales, down from 60.8% in 2024. Online orders took 2.93 days to deliver on average.

**Questions for the leadership team**
- What changed in the United States, where sales went from $158.8M to $126.3M, and is it the same customers buying less or fewer customers?
- TV and Video lost 35.9%: is that range, price or availability?
- With online share down to 55.3%, are stores winning back sales or is online losing them?
